purpose: frozen V9-A diagnosis with real DPC plus Open-Meteo inputs and same-period ERA5T targets
limitations: ERA5T is a gridded reference rather than error-free in-situ truth.
The seven-day period is a compatibility and domain-shift diagnosis, not a new training or model-selection set.
Availability/error correlations are descriptive and do not establish causality.
Dense ERA5T persistence uses stronger information unavailable to the operational model.

v9_a_vs_v7_b.definition: 1 - candidate_RMSE / baseline_RMSE; positive means candidate is better

v9_a_era5t_proxy_vs_v7_b_era5t_proxy.definition: 1 - candidate_RMSE / baseline_RMSE; positive means candidate is better

v9_a_vs_v9_reconstruction_persistence.definition: 1 - candidate_RMSE / baseline_RMSE; positive means candidate is better

v9_a_vs_v7_reconstruction_persistence.definition: 1 - candidate_RMSE / baseline_RMSE; positive means candidate is better

v9_a_vs_dense_era5t_persistence.definition: 1 - candidate_RMSE / baseline_RMSE; positive means candidate is better

operational_input_penalty.definition: operational-input MSE minus complete ERA5T point-input MSE; positive indicates domain/missingness penalty

availability_relationship.interpretation: negative correlation means more valid DPC cells coincide with lower error; association is not causation
